newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU says deeply regrets Lebanon violence.
newsitem.headline: EU says deeply regrets Lebanon violence.

text.p: The European Union said on Tuesday it deeply regretted the resurgence of violence in Lebanon and urged all parties to respect an earlier agreement not to target civilians.
"The European Union presidency deeply regrets that once again innocent civilians are victims of violence in the Middle East," the Luxembourg foreign ministry said in a statement.
Luxembourg currently holds the rotating EU presidency.
The statement said the EU called on all parties to respect an April 1996 ceasefire under which Israel and pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas agreed not to target civilians.

Ten people were killed and dozens wounded on Monday when pro-Israeli Lebanese militiamen shelled the southern port of Sidon and six Katyusha rockets struck Jezzine, a Lahd stronghold outside an Israeli-held occupation zone in south Lebanon.
On Tuesday, dozens of rockets were fired from Lebanon into northern Israel, injuring at least one civilian.
Hizbollah has been trying to oust Israeli troops and militiamen of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army from a 15-km (nine-mile) deep border zone inside Lebanon.
